borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: <div>The single storey component of the proposed rear extension, by reason of scale, siting and design, would be an undesirable addition which would cause an unacceptable level of overshadowing, loss of daylight and overbearing impacts to the adjoining dwellings This would result in a harmful impact to the amenity currently enjoyed by neighbouring occupiers. As such, the proposal fails to protect residential amenity and constitutes un-neighbourly development. It therefore fails to accord with the following policies which seek to ensure that development proposals protect residential amenity:&nbsp;<br></div><div><br></div><div><p><span pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="" style="font-size: 10.5pt;">- National Planning Policy Framework&nbsp;</span>National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (December 2024);<o:p></o:p></p><p><span pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="" style="font-size: 10.5pt;">- Policies D6, DMD1, DMD5 and DMSI3 of the London Plan (March 2021);</span></p><p><span pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="" style="font-size: 10.5pt;"><span pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="" style="font-size: 10.5pt;">- Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD5 of&nbsp;</span>The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan 2037 (September 2024);</span></p><p class="MsoNormal"><span pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="" style="font-size: 10.5pt; line-height: 14.98px;">- The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)</span></p><p class="MsoNormal"></p><p><br></p></div>

<div>The proposed development, by reason of its scale, siting, design, bulk and mass, would be an undesirable addition, representing an overly dominant and excessive addition that is not subservient to the modest semi-detached dwelling.
